reviews.review: This is one of the best games ever made.

Really wish I would have gotten the legendary edition so my DLC that I PAID FOR would work properly. However it's still a bit frustrating on the whole ease-dropping conversation to get side quests or additional 'lore' how I have to completely leave that area or level and return repeatedly. Soo even if I had the game working properly with allowing my PAID DLC to work, I don't know how much less aggravating some areas would actually be.. but maybe if everything I paid for would actually work, I'd be more lenient on the annoyance of the back and forth ease-dropping ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Also I have only played about 12/20 hours into the game, but it's logged over 45 because every time I close out it has the biggest issues just reopening the game, so I was just leaving it run so I would not have to deal with it, but as it was making other things run slow or in low quality I exited it, which made it lock up my computer.. I'm not sure I even want to continue this game, which sucks because for the most part I really enjoyed the first two games, regardless of having similar issues with DLC in ME2.

I could just say "It's bad" and move on but I'm enough of a loser that I'll vent about a 10 year old game that I'm still SEETHING over.

Don't ever listen to any redditor that says "IT'S A GREAT GAME ONLY THE ENDING IS BAD"

The vast bulk of the game is a rushed mess of dumbed down mechanics, bad writing and forced combat sections occasionally sprinkled with story and character bits that feel somewhat like the old games and all adds up to deliver us a game that's almost a textboook example of missed potential and studio meddling.


Ignoring the ending, lets talk about what parts of the story that completely drop the ball

The game introduces a Deus Ex Machina and insists that you have to use it to defeat the Reapers with the game schizophrenically saying "WE CAN'T EVEN FIGHT THEM WITHOUT THIS" and then the next mission saying that resistance forces on planets are keeping the Reapers back.........................somehow? which is it? That's also ignoring the fact that you've killed reapers in past games before and even help kill some in this game as well.
It feels like the writers weren't in communication with one another on this aspect of the story at all.

What they do with Cerberus is just flat-out bad turning a morally grey secretive organisation from ME2 and transforming them into an unstoppable bunch of evil morons that have unlimited reserves of men and weapons out of nowhere, regardless of what you picked in ME2.

90% of your squadmates from past games have almost nothing really important to do because Bioware didn't have time to provide anything really meaty gameplay or storywise in case they were dead or a new player was starting with the 3rd game (A consumer base that Bioware really REALLY pushed for in the marketing of the game even adding "Story and Combat" modes that let you skip either one).

All squadmates now have the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Zaeed and Kasumi ME2 style "conversations" as the default in ME3 along with completely removing the neutral options from dialogue choices AND having Shepard automatically respond to stuff way WAY more than the past games.


Stylistically the game is also a step backwards from past entries as well.
The gritty lived in style of ME2 and the Syd Mead inspired aesthetics of ME1 are all thrown in the bin and replaced with a generic shiny sci-fi look with an ugly plastic sheen on everything. The tweaks they made to the engine/character models also means characters from older games can end up looking completely different and in some cases outright unrecognisable from their past appearances with older character suddenly looking 30 years younger (Kelly and Bailey being some of the worst examples)

Gameplay wise it's probably the most polished of the 3 but it often falls into the Dragon Age 2 problem of forcing combat encounters out of a worry that the player will get bored if they don't kill something every 5 minutes with garbage turret sections thrown in all over the place (many of which you don't even need to fire a single shot it's literally just the game giving you ♥♥♥♥ to shoot at for a set amount of time before the game activates a level transition to a new area).

Multiplayer is "fine" if bare bones but it took resources away from the single player so it can piss off.

The DLC's range from meh to decent but the premise of the Citadel DLC simply doesn't work within the story because Bioware insisted they had to keep their crap endings that will almost certainly be retconned in the upcoming Mass Effect 4 if that ever comes out.

Everyone knows the ending is crap and that Kai Leng is a Sonic fanfic tier edgelord of bad writing so I won't beat that dead horse anymore than I already have.



TL:DR 10 years later and I'm still SEETHING
